title: Behavioral Equivalence Cannot See Dormant Logic: A Pre-Registered Negative Result from a Five-Arm Comparison of PLC Command Gates on a Simulated PLC
description: WACE Technical Report TR-2026-01 (defensive publication, released 2026-09-21). A pre-registered five-arm comparison of PLC command gates on a simulated PLC: adding a behavioral-equivalence check did not reduce hazardous false passes (23 of 280 in both arms); four of eight person-exposure false passes were motor-start commands issued after an interlock had been removed, a class that observation-based freshness checks cannot see. A static program-signature check must precede any behavioral check; on protocols without a program signature (Modbus) the gate cannot see this class of change. Results are from a simulated PLC on one machine; no physical PLC comparison is included. The report publishes its run ledger, denominators and excluded rows, and states its known limitations.
